Warehousing

Luân chuyển tồn kho

A systematic inventory management practice ensuring older stock is distributed or sold before newer stock, reducing spoilage and obsolescence—typically documented as FIFO or FEFO procedures.

Quick answer: A systematic inventory management practice ensuring older stock is distributed or sold before newer stock, reducing spoilage and obsolescence—typically documented as FIFO or FEFO procedures.

Quick answer

A systematic inventory management practice ensuring older stock is distributed or sold before newer stock, reducing spoilage and obsolescence—typically documented as FIFO or FEFO procedures.

Why it matters

Luân chuyển tồn kho matters because it supports clear communication in Warehousing contexts for Freight Forwarders, Supply Chain Managers, and Customs Brokers. It also connects to aviation training and exam language such as FIATA Diploma, CILT Certification, and IATA DGR.

Questions and answers

Questions and answers

What is Luân chuyển tồn kho?

In this glossary, Luân chuyển tồn kho refers to: A systematic inventory management practice ensuring older stock is distributed or sold before newer stock, reducing spoilage and obsolescence—typically documented as FIFO or FEFO procedures.

How is Luân chuyển tồn kho used in logistics?

In logistics communication, this term appears in contexts such as: "Các quy trình luân chuyển tồn kho nghiêm ngặt như FIFO rất quan trọng để giảm lãng phí và đáp ứng quy định an toàn thực phẩm tại các trung tâm phân phối."

Why does Luân chuyển tồn kho matter in logistics?

Luân chuyển tồn kho matters because it supports clear communication in Warehousing contexts for Freight Forwarders, Supply Chain Managers, and Customs Brokers. It also connects to aviation training and exam language such as FIATA Diploma, CILT Certification, and IATA DGR.

What category does Luân chuyển tồn kho belong to?

Where does this definition come from?

This definition is sourced from Incoterms 2020 (ICC), FIATA, IATA DGR, WCO and published by Protermify Logistics as a static logistics reference page.

Definition

A systematic inventory management practice ensuring older stock is distributed or sold before newer stock, reducing spoilage and obsolescence—typically documented as FIFO or FEFO procedures.

Operational example

Strict stock rotation protocols like FIFO are vital for minimizing waste and meeting food safety compliance in distribution centers.
